  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]

  WHY: A regression in `triage_supersede_candidate`, `triage_supersede_stale_issue`, the `supersede` stage, the widened dedup `--jq` projection, or the post-step wiring at `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` lines 743-746 would merge with CI green; minimax rated this BLOCKER and the other three rated it MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- tests/test_assemble_prompt.py:430-454 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_unblock_judge_prompt_and_template_offer_pr_check_green_not_operator_rerun` (line 442) is defined after `def main()` and `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`, so it is never collected when CI runs the file directly (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 2308).
  WHY: Drift between `prompts/mode-judge-unblock.txt` and `prompts/_templates/mode-judge-unblock.txt`, or removal of the new hard rule or the `pr_check_green` entry, would go undetected; minimax rated this BLOCKER and the others MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:229-234 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `triage_supersede_stale_issue` adds the `ai:closed` label before the close PATCH, and a failed close does not remove the label, so the issue stays open while carrying a terminal label.
  WHY: `reconcile_wave_issue_status()` in `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py` lines 2367-2370 treats `ai:closed` as closed even when the issue is open, which breaks the requirement that a failed close keeps both issues open; sonnet rated this NIT (conf 3, matches the existing label-then-close order in `check_triage_resolution.py`), the other four rated it MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:207-237, 605-628, 1020-1043 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `supersede` stage comments on, labels and closes the old issue as `not_planned` using the collect-time snapshot in `triage_metadata.json`, without re-reading the issue's state or labels before writing.
  WHY: An issue that is resumed (`ai:blocked` removed), reopened, or closed (for example by the resolution gate) during diagnose/route is still superseded on stale evidence; every reviewer rated this NIT (minimax also raised it under IMPLICIT-EXECUTION at 229-234, citing writes wrapped in `|| true` with no retry or idempotency).
- scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:118-144, 372-377 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `job_failed_at_checkout()` identifies the checkout step only by its display name (`CHECKOUT_STEP_NAME="Checkout repository"` line 73, `CHECKOUT_STEP_PREFIX="Run actions/checkout"` line 74), so a PR step with that name that emits checkout-fetch `::error::` annotations is classified as `checkout_fetch` and triggers the privileged rerun.
  WHY: Step display names and annotation text are PR-controlled, and the once-per-head cap limits how often this happens but does not prevent it; gemini, luna and zai rated it MAJOR, minimax rated it NIT (a continuation of the existing `runner_shutdown`/`action_resolution` pattern), and sonnet considered and dropped it, so the highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21526-21530 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: In `_stall_check_triage_resolution_gate`, the healing note at line 21528 always says the gate "verified the fix on the default branch and closed the issue", even for `path=open_head` resolutions through `_verify_open_head`.
  WHY: Every open-head resolution records a false explanation for operators (observability only); all three rated it NIT.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:174-178 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `triage_supersede_candidate` Python heredoc trusts `author_association` (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR User, or `github-actions[bot]`) instead of comparing `user.login` with the authenticated bot identity.
  WHY: A stale, hand-filed `ai:check-triage` issue from a maintainer or collaborator can be closed as `not_planned`, which widens the trust boundary beyond the spec without an off-switch.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:339-352 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_pr_check_green_condition` reuses `${RUNTIME_DIR}/triage_resolution.json`, which `unblock_check_triage_resolved()` writes per item without an atomic rename, so a hold check can read another item's verdict.
  WHY: Item A's hold could apply item B's verdict if the reads and writes interleave; a per-issue file, a lock, or `mv -f` would close the window.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
